expectations.text: Warns that silently rerouting retired-version calls keeps apps running while their behavior changes underneath them - a silent-drift failure, not a safe outcome.
expectations.evidence: "your app keeps running while its behaviour changes underneath you."

expectations.text: Recommends a hard cutoff as the default enforcement style at the sunset date.
expectations.evidence: "every /v1/* request returns 410 Gone."

expectations.text: Specifies that the retired version should return a clear, described error rather than silence or connection drops.
expectations.evidence: The body is application/problem+json with code, retired_at, migration_guide_url and support_contact.

expectations.text: Recommends a grace period after the sunset date returning 410 Gone so callers get a diagnosable error.
expectations.evidence: "The 410 response continues for 30 days after [D]."

expectations.text: Includes a machine-findable pointer to the replacement version (successor-version link relation or equivalent link in the error body).
expectations.evidence: "Each response carries Link: <…/v2/…>; rel=\"successor-version\"."

expectations.text: Points out that routing /v1 requests into the /v2 handler sends callers onto an incompatible contract - the plan delivers the breaking change silently; where fall-forward exists as a documented practice it routes to the oldest still-accessible version, not the newest.
expectations.evidence: "Meta falls forward to an older, compatible version. This plan jumps to a new contract, which is riskier."

expectations.text: If a fall-forward style is retained at all, requires it to be documented loudly and states that documented is not the same as noticed - documented silent rerouting still generates persistent complaints about behavior drift.
expectations.evidence: Fall-forward is rejected outright, and the 'documented is not the same as noticed' point is never made.

expectations.text: States the chosen enforcement style must be written into the policy, and that if enforcement differs per API surface, both styles must be written down.
expectations.evidence: No statement that enforcement style must be written down or that per-surface differences need both documented. It only scopes the section to REST /v1.

expectations.text: Frames deprecation as staged (announce, deprecate, sunset, removal) rather than a single October event.
expectations.evidence: The transcript has pre-sunset, sunset, grace and removal pieces but never frames them as the announce, deprecate, sunset, removal stages.

expectations.text: Recommends shipping a Deprecation header on v1 responses ahead of the sunset, noting it can ship before or independently of the sunset date and changes no behavior.
expectations.evidence: It recommends the `Deprecation` header (RFC 9745) but does not say it can ship independently of the sunset date or that it changes no behavior.

expectations.text: Recommends a Sunset header carrying the firm retirement timestamp on the deprecated version's responses only.
expectations.evidence: "`Sunset: [D]` (RFC 8594) once the date is firm" on v1 responses.

expectations.text: Requires migration support (migration guide, tooling where feasible, support channel) as part of the plan - announcing the sunset and leaving integrators to figure it out is named as a failure mode, not a middle ground.
expectations.evidence: "A migration guide covering each v1→v2 change with concrete steps, plus a support channel."
